item.description:
• Editing a collection made without a search, named like a series ("Legend of Zelda"), fills in the series' search and turns on adding new matching games, ready to save
  • "Start from a Series" is offered while editing a collection without a search, keeping its name and logo

• The collection editor lists its games in a column beside the settings, and always fits on the screen however many games there are
  • "But not" now also takes out games already in the collection: "Mario, but not Party" unticks the Mario Party games, ready to save

• Eight more systems, each with its About page and BIOS list: NAOMI 2, NAOMI GD-ROM (now its own system), Model 2, ST-V, Gaelco, 64DD, Satellaview and SuFami Turbo
  • NAOMI lists its game BIOS sets, and Settings › BIOS can show systems you have no games for
  • Arcade boards scrape from their own ScreenScraper systems, and every MAME board's games get their real titles instead of their set names
  • Verify Games can check a single system (from its overview or the sidebar), and checks arcade sets too against FinalBurn Neo or MAME's list, which it can download for you: missing or wrong ROMs, parents, BIOS and disc images
  • The verify report lists games by name, the verified ones included
  • Replace Existing Info now shows the new images straight away, and ScreenScraper scrapes videos too

• BIOS files are checked by MD5 against known good dumps: verified, or not a known dump with the expected and found checksums and a Compare view; a missing file that's in the BIOS folder under another name is found, with Use It to copy it in place
  • Recently Added in the sidebar and Cabinet Mode, and Date Added as a sort order
  • The toolbar's dice (⌥⌘R) picks a game at random from the ones shown
  • File › Library Statistics: totals, play time by month, the most played games, and each system's games, play time and room on disk

• Tools › Verify Games checks each game against No-Intro's DAT files (from DAT-o-MATIC, loose or as the daily pack's zip, in the Emulation folder's DATs folder): verified, differs from No-Intro's dump, or not listed
  • The verdict shows in the game panel; the report lists the games to look at, system by system
  • Good dumps filed under names of their own can be renamed to No-Intro's names, with their media, gamelist entries and saves, keeping play history and collections
  • Zipped games are checked from the zip's own checksums, without unpacking; cartridge headers (NES, SNES, Atari 7800, Lynx) are handled

• Save backups: Tools › Back Up Saves, or weekly from Settings › General; a zip of saves, save states, collections and gamelists, the newest five kept
  • File › Import Collection… (or a drop) reads ES-DE and Batocera custom collections (custom-Name.cfg)
  • Collections can choose games by genre, players, release years and favorites, with or without title words
  • A game taken out of a collection stays out after it's compressed
  • Unzipped copies of games are kept under 2 GB, the ones played longest ago going first
  • ScreenScraper matches a zipped game by the ROM inside
  • A deleted collection doesn't come back from a leftover folder

• Collections can take their logo from a folder of series logos (Settings › General › Collections), named like ES-DE and Batocera themes' (mario.png, zelda.png…).
  • Click a collection's logo to replace it, drop a picture on it, or use Add Logo… when it has none.
  • Drop an exported collection folder, or its collection.json, on the library to import it; a folder copied into Emulation/Collections joins the library by itself, with its logo.
  • A picture dropped on the library by mistake is no longer imported as a PICO-8 game.

• New Tools menu: Tidy Up, Compress Games, the selected game's conversion, removing unzipped copies, and a BIOS check.
  • Compress Games: disc games to CHD (now PSP too) and cartridge games to ZIP, losslessly, with a report to approve first. A CHD can be turned back into CUE/BIN, GDI or ISO.
  • The game panel shows a disc game's format, tracks, size, compression and SHA-1.
  • A compressed game keeps its favorite, play history, collections and gamelist info.
  • Fixed a crash at launch when the library window had been saved narrow.
  • Series templates are listed by name, and the BIOS list follows the library's order (by maker, then release).

• Tidy Up can compress disc games to CHD (PS1, PS2, Saturn, Sega CD, Dreamcast, PC Engine CD, 3DO, Neo Geo CD, PC-FX): one lossless file per disc, usually 30–60% smaller, checked before the originals go to the Trash. Uses MAME's chdman, which Attic can install with Homebrew.
  • RetroAchievements: sign in once in Settings › Emulators, and games earn achievements in RetroArch, DuckStation and PCSX2, with an optional hardcore mode. Only a sign-in token is kept, in the Keychain.

• A game's video plays, muted, in the side panel after a moment on it, with a button for the sound (Settings › General can turn previews off).
  • Play counts, last played, playtime and favorites from ES-DE and Batocera gamelists are brought in once, so your history carries over.
  • Settings › BIOS lists every system you have games for and what its emulator needs, missing files first.
  • Multi-disc games show as one game: Attic writes their .m3u playlist. The .bin tracks of .cue games no longer show up as games.
  • Tidy Up can find duplicate games (other regions, revisions, betas, a zip of the same game) and keep the best copy; off unless you tick it.
  • Standalone emulators (DuckStation, Dolphin, PCSX2, RPCS3, xemu, Vita3K, shadPS4) are checked for updates and update from Settings › Emulators.
  • Drop a PS Vita .vpk, .pkg (with its zRIF) or firmware to install it in Vita3K, or a dumped PS4 game folder to file it under PlayStation 4.

• Collections search by several terms at once and can leave some out ("Super Mario, Mario Bros" but not "Kart, Tennis"), optionally on one system, with every match listed to untick before adding.
  • Start a collection from about 55 popular series, each with a tuned search and how many of your games it finds.
  • Collections remember their search: Edit Collection (toolbar, File menu or right-click) runs it again or changes it, takes games out, and can add new matching games by itself after each library scan.
  • Collections sort by system, then release date, so a series reads in order (in Cabinet Mode too).
  • With a collection open, the side panel shows its pictures, game count and years, systems, search and play history. Give a collection a logo and artwork; Cabinet Mode shows the logo.
  • Each collection is saved as a folder in Emulation/Collections, with its pictures: it travels with your games, comes back if the library is reset, and can be exported and imported (File menu).
  • File menu: Add Games… (⌘O), Refresh Library (⌘R), Show ROMs Folder, Import/Export Collection; New Window, which crashed, is gone. A Refresh button sits in the toolbar, and the Game menu can open a game's manual.
  • Attic's folders are now Media, Gamelists and Collections beside ROMs, BIOS, Saves and the rest; ES-DE's downloaded_media and gamelists are renamed on first launch.

• Tidy Up starts with Analyze…: a dry run that lists every change (media to move, gamelists to fix, covers and manuals to compress, and what goes to the Trash and why, with sizes). Untick any part, then tidy up.
  • Games show their box art again instead of ES-DE's mix image; mix images and title screens are no longer kept (a game with nothing else keeps one as its cover or screenshot).
  • Dropped folders no longer bring mix images or title screens along.

• Drag games onto Attic: on a sidebar system, on the library, or a whole folder (a system folder like atari2600, or a full roms folder). Each game goes to the right ROMs folder, with its covers, videos, manuals and gamelist, and a progress bar shows the import.
  • New systems: PlayStation Vita (Vita3K, which adds installed games by itself) and PlayStation 4 (shadPS4), plus ScummVM, DOOM, Quake, EasyRPG, Sharp X68000, NEC PC-88 and PC-98, PICO-8, TIC-80, WASM-4, Arduboy, Commodore VIC-20, Plus/4 and 128, ZX81 and the classic Macintosh.
  • ROM-hack folders (nesh, snesh, n64h, gbah, genh, psxh…) show as systems of their own and play like the system they're made for.
  • All media now lives in downloaded_media beside your games, ES-DE style; scraped and picked covers are saved there as HEIC, and earlier ones move over by themselves.
  • Settings › General › Tidy Up moves Batocera media and gamelists into place, cleans gamelists, compresses covers and heavy manual scans, and moves other apps' leftovers to the Trash.
  • Attic makes a ROMs folder for every system it knows, each with a _sysinfo.txt saying what goes there.
  • A Manual button opens a game's PDF manual.

• Games no longer launch into a crash when a required BIOS is missing: Attic says which files are needed and opens the right folder (Play Anyway is there for dumps named differently).
  • BIOS files show one Found/Missing row each on every system, and follow the emulator you chose (PCSX ReARMed and YabaSanshiro need fewer).
  • PlayStation 2: PCSX2's own Mac app replaces Play!, and PS2 BIOS dumps put straight in the BIOS folder are moved where PCSX2 looks for them.
  • The system panel shows the ROM folder, file types, maker and year, and suggests an emulator to install when the system has none (in System Settings too).
  • The sidebar groups systems by maker, with a sort menu next to the sidebar button (manufacturer, name, release year, number of games) and an option to hide systems with no games.
  • Remove a system from the library (right-click, or System Settings); its files stay, and Settings › General can add it back.
  • Each system's ROMs folder gets a short _sysinfo.txt; Settings › General can move ES-DE's and Batocera's info files to the Trash.

Attic now has its own icon, and every system its logo.

  • System Settings: right-click a system, or use the button in the right panel, to choose how its games look and play. "Default" shows what the emulator does when left alone.
  • Looks: sharp pixels, CRT TV (flat or curved), handheld LCD, none, any preset from RetroArch's shader library, or your own .slangp file.
  • Retro look by default (Settings › Emulators › Shaders): CRT scanlines for 2D consoles and arcade, an LCD grid for handhelds.
  • 3D systems: internal resolution, widescreen, and PGXP geometry correction for PlayStation, in RetroArch cores, DuckStation and Dolphin.
  • Integer scaling, run-ahead to cut input lag, rewind, resume where you left off, no more sprite flicker on 8- and 16-bit consoles, and Game Boy Advance screen colors.
  • Attic can download libretro's shader pack and tells you when there's a newer one.
  • The right panel shows the selected system: its logo, emulator, BIOS files (found or missing), play history, and buttons for System Settings and scraping.
  • System logos by Dan Patrick, also in Cabinet Mode and above each game's details.
  • Clicking an empty spot in the grid, or picking another system, deselects the game.
  • The toolbar no longer runs over the right panel.

RomsBox is now called Attic, and Big Box is now Cabinet Mode.

  • Your library, collections, settings, artwork and scraper keys carry over from RomsBox automatically.
  • Attic updates itself: Attic › Check for Updates…, and Settings › General › Updates.
  • Scraped screenshots are shown at the top of the detail panel.
  • Only each system's ROM file types are listed in the library.
